evidence.ai_role: Four random forests predicted disruption or preservation of four LAG-3 interactions from molecular fingerprints and physicochemical descriptors; their combined selectivity score ranked compounds for successive experimental batches, with retraining on returned results.
evidence.tested: BVX-01 bound human LAG-3 at 42 +/- 4.0 nM. The study reports biochemical selectivity, donor-derived neuronal assays, receptor-dependence tests and pathology reductions in PS19 and 5xFAD mice, with two cohorts per model and 12 mice per arm.
evidence.unknown: No human clinical efficacy is established. The full preclinical cascade rests on one compound; the role of each disrupted interaction in mouse pathology remains unresolved. Additional-target tests stopped at primary screening. The exploratory chemist comparison had unequal access to candidates and lacked contemporaneous proof of chemist-selection timing.

source_review.scope: Primary v1 PDF Results, Discussion and Materials and Methods, including selection policy, biochemical and cellular tests, mouse-study design and limitations; bioRxiv API version/date/abstract metadata. Supplementary files and repository commitments were not independently audited.

summary: A November 24, 2026 bioRxiv preprint reports that Bivexia used random-forest predictions of four protein-interaction assays to select BVX-01, a small molecule that disrupted LAG-3 interactions with tau and amyloid-beta while preserving two other tested interactions. The authors report nanomolar LAG-3 binding, activity in donor-derived neurons, and reduced pathology readouts in two mouse models, with two cohorts per model. This is preclinical evidence from the discovery study, not peer-reviewed or independent confirmation or evidence of clinical benefit; the full cascade rests on one compound, and broader target campaigns stopped at primary screening.
title: Bivexia selects an interaction-selective LAG-3 inhibitor tested in mouse models
